identity.description: The monetary companion to the transaction BTYD models: a customer's average transaction value is Gamma-distributed around a latent mean that is itself Gamma-distributed across customers. Produces the conditional expected average profit per transaction (empirical-Bayes shrinkage of the customer's observed average toward the population), and — composed with a fitted BG/NBD or Pareto/NBD — discounted customer lifetime value.

axes.taskNote: UNCERTAINTY (U2/U3): same family flag — no `clv` task value exists; `regression` (expected monetary value) is the honest nearest fit here and needs no survival secondary (no dropout submodel in Gamma-Gamma).
axes.learningTypeNote: UNCERTAINTY (judgment call): a hierarchical empirical-Bayes density model of observed spend with no held-out label — Unsupervised chosen; 'Supervised with target = monetary_value' is the defensible alternative reading. Flagged for the family reviewer / U3.

consumes.note: consumed VIA the same Doc-2-placed event-log→RFM featurizer, run with monetary aggregation; the fitter's true input is the (frequency, monetary_value) pairs of REPEAT customers only (frequency > 0 — lifetimes docs are explicit). The numeric dtype (transaction amount) is REQUIRED here, unlike the sibling fitters. portTypeProposal (U2): `rfm-summary`. targetSpec `none` — no label separate from the observed spend the likelihood is over

a FITTED bg_nbd/pareto_nbd — lifetimes' customer_lifetime_value(transaction_prediction_model, ...) takes the sibling MODEL OBJECT, not its scores. Optional: unbound, the fitter still emits per-transaction expected spend; bound, it additionally emits discounted CLV. dataShape 'n/a' is deliberate — a model-reference port has no data shape; the template enum has no fitting value (template-fit gap, FLAGGED for U2)

emits.note: two modes on one port: (1) conditional_expected_average_profit — empirical-Bayes shrinkage of the customer's observed average spend toward the population mean p·v/(q−1); (2) with the optional trained-model input bound, customer_lifetime_value — per-customer discounted CLV over a predict-time horizon + discount_rate. UNCERTAINTY (U2): whether CLV deserves a port distinct from generic `score`
the fitted (p, q, v) ARE meaningful outputs (family truth: paramsAsOutput): they define the population spend distribution, with E[spend] = p·v/(q−1) — which requires q > 1 to exist

penalizer_coef.note: L2 penalty on (p, q, v); stabilizes small-cohort fits

q_constraint.note: constrains q > 1 so the population mean p·v/(q−1) exists; lifetimes fit-time flag — turn on when the unconstrained fit lands q ≤ 1

invariances.why: inverse sense, as across this family: monetary_value must stay in raw positive currency units — centering/standardizing produces non-positive values outside the Gamma support; a pure currency-unit rescale is absorbed by v. FLAGGED for U3: the boolean cannot express 'requires raw units'
log-transforming spend changes the Gamma-on-raw-spend commitment into a different (log-normal-like) model — the fit is not equivalent
the likelihood needs an observed (frequency, monetary_value) pair per repeat customer; NaN means the featurizer emitted a non-repeat customer or a defect — reject, don't impute
covariate-free — spend heterogeneity enters only through the Gamma prior on latent means

three commitments: spend Gamma-distributed around a latent per-customer mean, latent means Gamma-distributed across customers, AND monetary value independent of purchase frequency — the third is the load-bearing, checkable one
per-customer sample is the handful of repeat purchases (often 1–5); shrinking those noisy averages toward the population is precisely what the hierarchical prior is for
assumes the spend process is stationary, so the shrunk per-customer mean extends to FUTURE transactions — that extension is the CLV use case

featureStats.why: the model ASSUMES spend is independent of purchase frequency (the Fader-Hardie check); a materially nonzero correlation biases the conditional means — the gate stat for this family member
only frequency > 0 customers have an observed average spend and enter the likelihood — this, not the cohort size, is the effective sample size
cross-customer coefficient of variation of average spend; the hierarchical prior exists to shrink noisy small-frequency averages — near-zero CV means the population mean alone would suffice

modelMetrics.why: predicted conditional average profit vs realized holdout average spend per customer — the monetary analogue of the calibration/holdout purchase check
model-implied E[spend] = p·v/(q−1) vs the observed cohort average — a cheap first-order misfit check, and undefined at q ≤ 1, which is itself the signal to constrain q

edgeCases.behavior: monetary_value is undefined (no repeat purchases to average) — invalid likelihood rows
edgeCases.note: fit on repeat customers only, per lifetimes documentation

edgeCases.behavior: outside the Gamma support — likelihood undefined
the independence assumption is violated; conditional expected spend is biased
population mean p·v/(q−1) undefined or negative — expected-spend outputs are garbage

driver.constructor: GammaGammaFitter(penalizer_coef=...).fit(frequency, monetary_value); CLV via .customer_lifetime_value(transaction_model, frequency, recency, T, monetary_value, time=..., discount_rate=...)
driver.depNote: UNCERTAINTY (dep choice): lifetimes is in maintenance mode; pymc-marketing's clv.GammaGammaModel is the maintained successor (heavier PyMC dep; MCMC fit non-deterministic). Sheet written against lifetimes; flagged for family-level review
driver.wrapperNeeds: the same upstream RFM featurizer with monetary aggregation, PLUS a frequency > 0 filter before fit; the CLV path additionally needs the fitted sibling transaction model bound to the optional trained-model input, and predict-time horizon + discount_rate arguments
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded fit; predictions are pure functions of (p, q, v) — safe to parallelize after fit

canBeSeeds.note: composes WITH bg_nbd/pareto_nbd — their trained-model emission feeds this fitter's optional input, and the composite emits discounted CLV on this score port

placementClaims.why: the RFM featurizer emits complete (frequency, monetary) pairs for repeat customers by construction; missing spend is unobservable, not imputable
log/power transforms of spend replace the Gamma-on-raw-spend commitment with a different model — the fitted (p, q, v) no longer mean what the CLV math needs
centering makes spend non-positive, outside the Gamma support; pure currency-unit changes are absorbed by v and need no preprocessing
no categorical covariates exist in the input contract — the model is covariate-free
